corrections.text: The article says kernel TLS is "now enabled by default" on Linux and FreeBSD when OpenSSL has been built with kernel TLS support, citing the Crystal 1.20 announcement. The announcement as archived on April 21, 2026 said kernel TLS is "supported by default" when OpenSSL was compiled with it and "enabled on the system (likely disabled by default)", for example with `modprobe tls` on Linux, which describes support rather than an enabled default.

Crystal 1.20.1, released on April 29, 2026 at 20:09 UTC after this article was published, lists "OpenSSL Kernel TLS support should be opt-in (#16897)" and "Fix issues in OpenSSL Kernel TLS (#16888)" among its bugfixes. The 1.20 announcement now carries the note "Kernel TLS is opt-in since 1.20.1 due to unresolved issues". The kernel TLS behaviour the article describes therefore does not apply to Crystal 1.20.1 or later.
